description: SPACE TRACE es un proyecto dedicado a investigar, identificar y dar a conocer los objetos, equipos y tecnologías que las misiones espaciales han dejado en la Luna, Marte y otros lugares del espacio, preservando la historia de la exploración espacial.
summary:
We developed an interactive website that tells the history and science behind the equipment NASA left behind on the Moon and Mars. The project is designed for elementary school children and preteens (ages 7 to 14).

When you open the site, the first thing you see is a space-themed screen that invites you to explore. From there, you can browse through tabs featuring videos, real photos of the Apollo landing sites, audio recordings from missions like Ingenuity, Apollo, and the Voyager Golden Record, as well as 3D models that can be viewed from every angle. In "Our Heroes," you get to meet each machine alongside the person who created it and discover what it accomplished up there. Games were also included so that our target audience can learn in a more interactive way.

We tackled the challenge by turning abandoned equipment into stories that can be explored and remembered using NASA's open resources.

We care about this because these machines are part of what humanity has achieved in space, and we want children to get to know them and feel inspired to learn more about science and engineering.
details:
Space Trace - UPRIT "Abandoned, Not Forgotten"

It is an interactive web platform aimed at children and preteens aged 7 to 14, seeking to bring them closer to the history and science behind the equipment NASA left behind on the Moon and Mars.

  • It turns public NASA information and archives into an interactive educational experience through photographs from Apollo missions, historical audio recordings, mini-games, and the "Our Heroes" section, which showcases the equipment and the people behind its creation.
  • It promotes dynamic learning, making it easier to understand scientific concepts and bringing children closer to the world of science and engineering.
  • To spark scientific curiosity and foster an early interest in astronomy, technology, and engineering, preserving the history of these important space achievements.
  • The tools that helped us were: HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript for web development, as well as official resources from NASA's open data portal.
  • It offers a different perspective: presenting this equipment not merely as abandoned machines, but as protagonists of great missions and human achievements. In doing so, it turns scientific information into an interactive educational experience.
  • The age of the target audience, the use of simple language without losing scientific rigor, intuitive navigation, the accuracy of information backed by official NASA sources, and cross-browser compatibility.
